input.brief: Hand-painted Iznik cini tiles made to order in a small atelier in Iznik; visitors come to choose pattern and colour in person

direction.name: Colour chapters
direction.idea: Every section is a chapter with its own flat colour, floor to ceiling. The page reads like a set of posters hung in a row, held together by one typeface and one grid. The colours are not decoration: they come from the subject (the brand's packaging, the artist's record sleeves, the product's own colour ways, the categories of the content) and each chapter's colour means that chapter. Decide the sequence like a designer orders a book: a strong opener, a quiet second, a surprise in the middle, a dark or very light closer.
direction.composition: Sections are full-bleed fields, each at least 90svh tall, butted directly against each other with no gap and no divider. Inside every field the same 12-column grid and the same margins apply, and each field holds one thing: a huge heading (8–12vw) with a small paragraph, or one photograph with a caption, or one list. Text colour is chosen per field for strong contrast (ink or paper, never grey). Headings start on the same left edge in every chapter, so the eye feels the system as colours change. The navigation and the footer take the colours of the first and last chapter.
direction.typography: One typeface in two weights. Headings very large and tight; body 18–20px. Because colour is loud, the type stays plain: no italics, no second face.
direction.colour: Four to six flat fields used at full strength, one per section, each with its assigned text colour. No tints, no gradients between them: the hard edge where two fields meet is the look.
direction.imagery: Sparing. One photograph or object per chapter at most, either cut out and sitting directly on the colour, or a plain rectangle with generous colour around it. Photographs should be simple enough not to fight the field.
direction.richness: Colour at scale. A whole screen of one saturated colour is rich on its own, so a chapter needs few elements; it still needs its content at full size, because a coloured screen with one small line on it reads as empty.
direction.pitfalls: Check contrast on every field with the palette's assigned ink. Do not put cards on the fields. Do not use more than six colours. Two neighbouring fields should differ clearly in lightness as well as hue.

hero.name: Colour field, two-ink statement
hero.blueprint: One saturated flat colour covers the whole viewport; there is no navigation bar and no image. Two short pieces of 15px text sit in the top corners on 3% margins: the wordmark at the left, the single action as a text link in the dark ink at the right. The statement starts 15% down, left-aligned from the 3% margin, in a soft heavy serif or a heavy grotesk at clamp(110px, 14vw, 220px), tracking -0.03em, leaded so tightly (0.82) that the two lines nearly touch. Line one is set in a pale ink and line two in a dark ink, the only two inks on the field; the pair fills the top 55% of the screen and the longer line reaches about 90% of the width. A long name may be broken across the two lines with a hyphen if the second half reads as a word of its own. In the bottom-right corner, right-aligned in a column 24% of the viewport wide, one supporting sentence at 17px in the pale ink. The bottom-left quarter stays empty colour.
hero.mobile: The same field. The corner texts stay at the top at 14px. The statement sets at 21vw on two lines from a 16px margin, starting at 16% of the height, pale line over dark line. The supporting sentence moves to the bottom-left at 16px across 80% of the width, ending 24px above the bottom edge. The middle fifth of the screen stays empty colour.
hero.headline: The name or a two-word statement over two lines, at most 8 characters per line at 21vw on a phone.

type.note: A soft geometric sans with wide round letters and relaxed joins, warm at semibold and easy at text size. Suits consumer apps, community products, cafes and small friendly brands.

palette.name: Report blocks
palette.note: A white base with flat blocks of orange, sage, acid yellow and black assigned to whole modules: figure tiles, quote panels and chapter bands. Text is black on every colour and off-white on black, and orange is also the button colour.

motion.name: Colour by chapter
motion.description: Each chapter is its own full-bleed field of one palette colour, so the ground changes exactly at section edges as you scroll, never as a global recolouring of the screen. The only movement: the fixed header (or the one pinned element) takes the ink of the chapter beneath it, switching with a 300ms colour transition as each edge passes under it. Do not drive the page background from an observer: in blind tests a page recoloured mid-section, with a paragraph sitting on two colours, read as broken twice.

sections.name: Staircase statement
sections.blueprint: On a flat dark or saturated field one sentence of 12–18 words is broken into five short lines at clamp(36px, 4.4vw, 64px), bold, leading 1.02, marked up as one paragraph (a statement, so it may run past two lines at this size). Each line starts further right than the one above: indents of 0, 6, 12, 18 and 24vw from a 4vw left margin, set with `padding-left` per line, so the block descends like stairs and ends near the 75% mark. Each line takes its own flat colour from the palette, or lines alternate between two inks. The block is vertically centred in a section 100svh tall. The right quarter (columns 10–12) holds two stacked photographs, each 3:2 and 20vw wide with a 16px gap, top-aligned with the first line. No heading; a two-line note at 15px sits at the bottom-left margin, on the first line's left edge. On a page without images, leave the right quarter empty.
sections.mobile: Five lines at 9vw (35px on a 390px screen) with indents of 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20vw, so the stair still reads on a 390px screen. The two photographs follow below as one row of two equal 3:2 frames. The note sits last, left-aligned.

sections.name: Photo tiles with label strips
sections.blueprint: Four columns with 12px gaps; every tile is a photograph with a filled label strip attached directly beneath it, the two forming one object like a print with its swing tag. The photograph is 1:1 or 4:5 with square corners. The strip is the same width, 84–96px tall with 12px padding, and holds two or three rows of text at 12–13px in the text face with tabular figures: row one spreads four short values evenly across the width with `justify-content: space-between`; row two puts a date at the left end and a time or place at the right end; row three names the maker or model. Strip and text colours change per tile through four palette pairs (dark on bright, bright on dark), so a uniform grid looks varied. Rows of tiles are 28px apart. A two- or three-word heading at 32px sits top-left, 40px above the grid. Holds 8–16 tiles.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 8px gaps. Strips keep two rows only: the four values wrap to two per row, and the date and place line is dropped. Text stays at 12px. The heading sits above at 24px. Colour pairs keep rotating so adjacent tiles never match.

sections.name: Accordion of tinted panels
sections.blueprint: A two-column introduction, then one horizontal accordion. Introduction: the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), in columns 1–5; one paragraph at 18px in columns 7–11. 64px below, a flex row across columns 1–12, 520px tall, of four to six panels with no gaps. The open stage is a panel taking about 58% of the width; the rest are vertical slivers sharing what remains. Order is carried by colour: the first stage is the darkest tone of one hue and each later stage is a lighter flat tint of it, so the row reads dark to light from left to right. A sliver shows only its stage name, rotated 90 degrees and reading upward, at 20px bold, anchored to its bottom-left. The open panel shows the name at 40px top-left, a 36ch paragraph at 18px bottom-left and, optionally, one photograph in its right half. Clicking a sliver opens it (flex-basis transition, 450ms).
sections.mobile: The accordion turns vertical: stages stack at full width as bars 64px tall in the same dark-to-light order, names set horizontally at 18px. The open stage expands to its content height with the paragraph at 17px. The first stage is open by default.

sections.name: One item per poster line
sections.blueprint: A short list set as a poster. Four to seven items (services, headline acts, courses, opening days) stack one per line at clamp(64px, 10vw, 150px) in the display weight, all capitals or all lowercase, leading 0.92, flush left at a 20px margin on a flat field. Its one detail (a price, a date, a time range) sits at the right margin on the same baseline at 18–20px with tabular figures, so the page has two alignments only: giant words left, small facts right. Items too long for one line at this size are shortened, not shrunk. Between items there is only the tight leading. Hovering an item swaps its ink for the accent. There is no heading: the first item starts 80px below the section top and the last ends 80px above the bottom. The list reuses the hero title's exact type size, so it reads as another poster.
sections.mobile: Items at 15vw, one per line, flush left with 16px margins. Each detail moves beneath its item at 15px, left-aligned, with 6px above and 22px below. If any single word is wider than the screen at 15vw, drop the whole list to 12vw rather than breaking a word.

sections.name: Plans that step up
sections.blueprint: Three plans as flat colour tiles whose heights step like a bar chart, so the bigger plan is literally bigger. The tiles sit in one row with 8px gaps, bottoms on a common base line, each 4 columns wide: the first 360px tall, the second 480px, the third 600px. Each has its own palette colour, no border and one shared radius. Inside, top-left with 28px padding: the plan name at 28px bold, the price at 56px beneath it, then what is included as plain lines at 17px (the taller tiles simply have room for more lines). The bottom 64px of every tile is a strip in a darker flat tone of that tile's colour, and the whole strip is the button with its label left-aligned. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw occupies the empty space above the two shorter tiles, top-left.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack full width in rising order, each as tall as its content, keeping its colour and its darker button strip along the bottom. Gaps of 8px. The heading leads at 9vw on two lines, and prices drop to 44px.

sections.name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
sections.blueprint: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.
sections.mobile: The strip is 110px tall and scrolls by touch. The heading follows at 9vw. The three cells stack as full-width filled blocks 60px tall with 8px gaps, the submit block last. Small print sits beneath the stack, left-aligned.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Paul Kalkbrenner
references.idea: Swiss poster typography for a techno artist: the name as one black line with a photo set inside it like a glyph, then every chapter gets its own flat colour and visible grid.
references.hero: Pure white viewport. The artist's name sits on one line at exact vertical centre in bold black neo-grotesk, about 10.4vw, spanning roughly 78% of the width with equal side margins. The space between first and last name is replaced by a small landscape black-and-white photo, x-height tall and resting on the baseline. Top-left is a tiny circular monogram; eight nav links in 13px bold are spread at even intervals across the right half of the top edge. Bottom edge: equaliser bars with a grey label over a track title at left, a three-line bold blurb starting just left of centre, a sound toggle hard right. About 85% is empty.
references.type: ABC Diatype Plus Variable only: bold at -0.05em tracking for display and 13.5px bold for everything functional. Display runs from 150px in the hero to about 44vw elsewhere per the digest. Tiny uppercase labels inside boxed cells; no second face, no italics.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #c5c5c5 #a7ff9c #ff6831 — Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange. Photos inside coloured sections are tinted to the section hue or kept black-and-white.
references.imagery: Portraits and live shots of the artist: full-bleed colour images between sections, a grainy monochrome portrait marked up as a vinyl disc, a green duotone car portrait, and a strip of small mixed-ratio thumbnails. Square corners throughout.
references.layout: Outer margins of only 4-8px; content hangs on a visible column grid with hairlines and boxed cells. Sections alternate between full-bleed photographs and flat colour fields, each arranged differently, so the rhythm is one poster after another.

sections.description: Two words stacked in bold grotesk at roughly 8vw, each preceded by a solid black circle about the height of the lowercase, the second line indented further right than the first. Thin horizontal and vertical hairlines cross the white field at baselines and column edges like a construction grid. Directly beneath is a single row of streaming-service logos spaced evenly edge to edge, then a full-bleed photograph.

Flat mid-grey field split in two. Left half: a square grainy monochrome portrait with a large thin circle drawn on it and a small grey dot at the centre, so the photo reads as a record. Right half: a row of three year tabs and a small link above a hairline, the album title in small bold caps, a short description lower down, and along the bottom two wide outlined cells side by side acting as buttons.

Acid-mint field introducing the tour list. A large photograph, recoloured as a green-and-black duotone, occupies only the top-right quadrant; the left half is left empty. Along the bottom a table header with three tiny uppercase column labels sits on a hairline spanning the full width, where the list of dates begins.

Orange field. A horizontally scrolling strip of small photographs of differing widths runs across the top, cropped by both edges. Below it one outlined rectangle spans the width, divided into three equal cells: two inputs and a submit action, each identified only by tiny centred uppercase text. Small-print lines sit under the left and right cells.

steal: Replace the space between the two words of a giant name with a small photo cropped to x-height.
Flood each chapter with one flat colour and tint its photograph to match as a duotone.
Build forms and button pairs as adjoining outlined cells with tiny uppercase labels instead of filled buttons.
references.media: The hero is almost pure type: the only picture is a 113x75 chip set inside the name, under 1% of the fold, that changes photo every 1-1.5s. Later, full-bleed bands with scrubbed parallax between sections, a square cover in one half beside an info column, a green duotone portrait docked right, a full-bleed photograph that exits through a pixel-block mask, a receding stack of square photos, and an auto marquee of small thumbnails; one YouTube embed, no native video, square corners and an 8s grain overlay.
references.motion: There is no preloader, only the name chip cycling and the equaliser bars bouncing, and Lenis and Barba run 12 ScrollTriggers with no pins: media wrappers parallax by yPercent, a ruled statement drifts sideways, full-bleed photo sections scrub at 0.3 to drive the pixel-block dissolve, and year digits roll like an odometer. Link characters roll over 0.5s with a per-character delay on the house curve cubic-bezier(.625,.05,0,1) (.7s and .35s tokens).

references.name: Anidachi
references.idea: A toy brand built from one custom modular wordmark and one 3D device, both of which change colour with each full-bleed candy-coloured section.
references.hero: A saturated sky-blue field covering the top 92% of the viewport. The custom modular wordmark is repeated in four stacked rows, each spanning the full width inside 30px margins, drawn tone-on-tone in a slightly lighter blue that brightens row by row toward the bottom, so the name works as wallpaper. A tiny white pixel-cat mark sits top-left; a white rounded button with blue text top-right. A 3D flower-shaped toy device hangs on a carabiner from the top edge at centre, barely entered on desktop and fully visible on mobile, where it covers the pattern. A pale ice section starts at the bottom edge.
references.type: AnidachiDisplay is custom modular lettering: monoline rounded strokes on a square grid, unicase forms, used at 7-10vw. Body and UI in Ease, a soft rounded geometric sans, at 20px. Text is always coloured to its section, never black.
references.colour: #24c0fe #eff9fb #b6c814 #ff6b2b #ffffff #000000 — Each section is one flat saturated field (sky blue, ice, chartreuse, orange) with type in a single contrasting tint of the same family or white. The 3D device is recoloured to match its section.
references.imagery: A glossy flower-shaped handheld with cream buttons and a small black screen showing pixel-art animal characters, hung from a metal clasp. Pixel sprites also appear loose on the page and as a giant low-contrast watermark.
references.layout: Full-bleed colour sections of one to two screens with 30px margins. Each holds one giant display phrase at an edge, one small text block, and the 3D device crossing section boundaries. Alignment shifts section to section: centred, left column, bottom-left.

sections.description: Pale ice section. Centred: the small mascot mark and wordmark in sky blue at about 9vw, followed by a two-line statement in the rounded sans at 7vw in the same blue. Below, a left column 370px wide holds a three-line 24px lead and small paragraphs, all blue on ice; a pixel-art cat sprite stands in the right half, and a pill-outlined email field with a round arrow button ends the block.

Chartreuse full-bleed section. A title in the modular display face runs edge to edge in white at about 10vw across the top. The 3D device, recoloured olive to match, hangs from its clasp at left-centre and overlaps a diagonal ribbon of translucent rounded-square tiles, each holding a tinted character, running from lower-left to upper-right and off the edge.

Solid orange section, almost empty. A three-line 14px white paragraph sits near the top, right of centre; the bottom-left holds a two-line hyphenated phrase in the display face at roughly 9vw, white, hugging the left margin and the bottom edge. The lower edge of the device intrudes from the section above.

Ice ground with an enormous pixel-art face in a barely darker green tint as a watermark filling the frame. Lime wordmark lower-left at about 300px wide, three stacked lime links at centre, one link at right, tiny copyright beneath the logo.

steal: Repeat the wordmark as tone-on-tone rows filling the hero, stepping the tint row by row, so the brand name is the background pattern.
Give every section one saturated colour, set all its text in a single contrasting tint, and recolour the 3D product to match.
Anchor a giant two-line display phrase to the bottom-left corner of an otherwise empty colour field, with one small paragraph far away at the top.

references.name: Seasats
references.idea: Calm, dusk-lit seascapes sell autonomous boats as serene instruments, and the navigation is a column of stacked colour swatches taken from that sea-and-sand palette.
references.hero: A 10px white frame surrounds everything. The left 84% is one rounded media panel: a dusk scene of a low, solar-decked vessel centred on mirror-flat water, with two larger hulls cropped by the panel's left and right edges. The headline is centred in the panel's upper third, two lines of white light-weight flared serif at 124px (8.6vw). A wordmark in custom wide techno lettering sits top-left; a white rounded button with mono caps and a dark-green square arrow sits bottom-centre. The right 14% is the menu: a full-height column of stacked flat colour blocks (blush, sage, then four darkening olives), each holding left-aligned 15px links, sub-items numbered 01 to 04.
references.type: seasonMix, a low-contrast serif-sans hybrid, light weight, sentence case, near-zero tracking, at 124px for the headline and about 40px for statements; seasonSans 16px for body and menu; supplyMono uppercase at 9 to 12px for buttons, tags and footer data.
references.colour: #a6b3bc #232323 #b7c8be #d6c4b8 #2c3620 #e2832a — Slate blues and lilac greys from the seascapes dominate; the menu adds blush, sage and olive blocks; the footer flips to a burnt-orange and rust scene. Text stays white.
references.imagery: Photoreal rendered footage of autonomous boats on glassy water at dusk: symmetrical, low horizon, lots of sky, full-bleed after the hero. Small square-cornered inset stills with mono tag labels float over the scene.
references.layout: Mostly full-viewport scenes with one centred text block each, at top or bottom, and the wordmark fixed top-left. Only the hero uses the framed panel-plus-menu split. A thin vertical progress line runs down the right edge.

sections.description: A pinned full-bleed scene shot from the boat's deck: the hull forms a dark symmetrical wedge rising from the bottom edge to a mast at centre, horizon at one-third. At top-centre six short statements are stacked, centred, at 16px; one is white and the others half opacity, and the highlight steps down the list on scroll. For each, small photo cards (150 to 220px wide, square corners, mono tag on the top edge) appear left and right of the mast.

A full-bleed aerial view of dark teal water with several small vessels scattered across the lower half and a faint horizon near the top. A single two-line statement in the light serif at about 40px sits centred near the bottom edge. Nothing else is on screen except the wordmark top-left and the thin progress line at right.

Colour inverts to a burnt-orange haze over rust-red terrain, with black silhouettes of hulls and a keel hanging from the top edge as if seen from below the surface. Mid-height: mono readouts at left reporting distance scrolled in metres and scroll speed in knots with a one-line quip; a link list at 16px in the centre; mono contact details at right. The wordmark fills the full width at the bottom, white, about 130px tall.

steal: Build the menu as a full-height column of stacked flat colour blocks sampled from the imagery, grouping links by block colour instead of by rules or headings.
List every claim at once, centred and dimmed, and move a single full-opacity highlight through the list on scroll while supporting images appear around a fixed subject.
Give the footer its own opposite-temperature scene and a live readout of how far and how fast the visitor scrolled, in the product's own units.
references.media: A dusk render of the vessel on still water, as a still, a 3s muted loop and a canvas layered together, fills an inset card at about 84% of the width beside a colour-band nav panel and goes full bleed once scrolled. Then a scroll-scrubbed frame sequence on a sticky stage with labelled photo cards floating at depth, small video thumbnails that grow into full-bleed chapter loops, a WebGL globe rising as a half-sphere from the bottom edge, and sticky product renders that turn with the scroll; 18 images, 6 videos, 8px corners on the hero frame and cards.
references.motion: The preloader wordmark's seven letters slide up out of their masks at 50ms steps, the framed hero arrives at 1.2s and the title fades in softly, settling after about 5s, and smooth scroll then runs 34 sticky elements with no pins: the flythrough is a scrubbed image sequence, a fixed background layer changes the ground per chapter, and the nav collapses to a slim right-edge rail. Title characters rise on cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1) (the house ease, 17 uses) with durations that shorten by 12ms per character, so the end of a word catches up with its start.
